title: Freezing the level size
options: The loop bound changes as nodes are polled and children are offered, so a level ends early or late and nodes from different levels get mixed together
Nothing: `q.size()` is re-evaluated but gives the same number
explanation: Take `[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]`. Level 1 starts with the queue `[9, 20]`. With a live bound: poll 9 (i=0), then check `1 < q.size()`, which is `1 < 1`, false, so the loop stops and 20 slips into the next "level". That next level then polls 20 and also 15. Reading the size once before the loop fixes which nodes belong to the current level.

title: Template: level-order BFS
prompt: Fill in the level-order template (root is already known to be non-null).
explanation: Freeze the level size before the loop, poll exactly that many nodes, and enqueue only non-null children. `ArrayDeque` throws on `offer(null)`, and the null check also keeps empty slots out of the level lists.

title: Drill: sum of each level
prompt: From memory (level-order BFS): return a list with the sum of the node values on each level, top to bottom. An empty tree returns `[]`.
hints: You need to know where one level ends and the next begins. What can you record right before you start processing a level?
BFS with a queue: `int size = q.size();`, then poll exactly `size` nodes, adding each value to a running sum.
Reset `sum = 0` at the top of each while-iteration and `res.add(sum)` after the inner for loop. Null-check the root and each child before offering.

solution.explanation: The frozen `size` makes each outer iteration handle exactly one level, so you accumulate inside the for loop and record after it. O(n) time; the queue holds at most one level plus part of the next, O(w) space where w is the tree's maximum width.
